guide.q.standard_vs_daily_listings: What's the difference between standard and daily listings?
guide.a.standard_vs_daily_listings: A standard listing is a one-off — attendees book a place and the capacity applies to the whole listing. A daily listing lets attendees pick a specific date when booking. The capacity limit applies separately to each date, so you can run the same listing every day with a fresh allocation.
guide.q.combine_multiple_listings: How do I combine multiple listings into one booking?
guide.a.combine_multiple_listings:
Join listing slugs with a + in the URL, e.g. /ticket/listing-one+listing-two. Attendees see a single form, fill in their details once, and book all selected listings in one go. If any are paid, they complete one checkout for the total.

The attendee gets a single ticket with one QR code covering all their listings. Their ticket page shows one card per listing. In the admin, they appear as one attendee linked to multiple listings.

If the listings have different contact-detail settings, the combined form asks for the union of all selected fields — so pairing an email-only listing with one that also collects a phone number will require both from every attendee. Fields always appear in the same order (email, phone, address, special instructions) regardless of which listings are combined.

To generate the link, open the Multi-booking link section on the Listings page and tick the listings you want to combine. The link updates as you select, and listings appear in the order you tick them.
guide.a.what_are_groups: Groups let you bundle related listings under a single URL. Create a group from the Groups page, then tick the groups a listing belongs to using the Group checkboxes on the listing form — a listing can be in more than one group at once. Share /ticket/your-group-slug and attendees see all active listings in the group on one page. All listings in a group must be the same type (all daily or all standard). Set an optional Max Attendees on the group to cap total bookings across every listing in it. If you add terms and conditions to a group, they replace the global T&Cs for that page.
guide.q.listing_date_and_location: What are the listing date and location fields for?
guide.a.listing_date_and_location: These are optional fields you can fill in when creating or editing a listing. The date is when the listing takes place (in your configured timezone) and the location is where it's held. Both are displayed on the attendee's ticket page so they know when and where to go. For daily listings, attendees already pick a date when booking, so the listing date field is more useful for standard (one-off) listings.
guide.q.max_tickets_per_purchase: What does 'max tickets per purchase' do?
guide.a.max_tickets_per_purchase: It controls how many tickets one person can book in a single transaction. For example, setting it to 4 lets someone book up to 4 places at once. The quantity dropdown on the booking form won't exceed this number or the remaining capacity, whichever is lower.
guide.a.allow_pay_more: When enabled, attendees can choose their own price instead of paying a fixed amount. The ticket price becomes a minimum. You can set a maximum price using the "Maximum Price" field — it must be at least {minPriceFormatted} more than the ticket price. If the ticket price is zero, it becomes a pay-what-you-want listing where attendees can optionally enter any amount up to the configured maximum.
guide.a.what_are_modifiers:
Modifiers change checkout prices without editing the base listing price. Open Modifiers to create discounts, surcharges, promo codes, returning-customer offers, or optional add-ons. A modifier can apply to the whole order, to specific listings, or to every listing in selected groups.

Each modifier has a trigger: Automatic applies whenever its rules match, Promo code applies when the buyer enters the matching code, and Optional add-on lets the buyer choose it on the booking form. You can also limit modifiers with a minimum order amount, minimum previous bookings, stock, and active/inactive status.
guide.a.how_modifier_values_work:
The Type decides how the Value is read:

  • Fixed amount: enter an amount in your currency. For example, 10 means a 10.00 charge or discount, depending on the Direction.
  • Percentage: enter the number only. For example, 10 means 10% of the in-scope subtotal. Percentages must be greater than 0 and at most 100.
  • Multiplier: enter the final multiplier factor. For example, 1.5 makes the in-scope subtotal 1.5x, 0.5 makes it half price, and 10 makes it 10x. Direction is ignored for multipliers because the factor itself decides whether the price rises or falls.

Modifiers are calculated from the original in-scope subtotal and do not compound on each other. The booking fee is then calculated from the final modified subtotal.
guide.a.registration_deadlines: Set a "closes at" date and time on your listing. After that moment, the booking form shows a "registration closed" message and no further bookings are accepted. If someone loaded the form before the deadline but submits after, their booking is also rejected.
guide.q.embed_booking_form: How do I embed the booking form on my website?
guide.a.embed_booking_form:
You only need one of the two embed codes shown on your listing page — not both:

  • Embed Script (recommended) — paste a single <script> tag and it creates the iframe for you with automatic resizing.
  • Embed Iframe — use this if your hosting platform blocks third-party scripts or if you want full control over the iframe styling yourself.

In Settings, add your website's domain to the embed hosts list to restrict which sites can embed your forms. If no hosts are listed, embedding is allowed from any site.
guide.q.manually_add_attendee: How do I manually add an attendee?
guide.a.manually_add_attendee: Open the listing page and scroll down to Add Attendee. Fill in the name and contact details, set the quantity, and submit. The attendee is added directly without needing to go through the booking form or payment flow. Useful for walk-ins, comps, or manual corrections.
guide.q.custom_redirect_after_booking: How do I set a custom redirect after booking?
guide.a.custom_redirect_after_booking: When creating or editing a listing, enter a URL in the "thank you URL" field. After a successful booking or payment, attendees are redirected to that address instead of seeing the default confirmation page. The URL must use HTTPS, or you can use a relative path starting with /.
guide.q.add_listing_image: How do I add an image to a listing?
guide.a.add_listing_image: When creating or editing a listing, use the image upload field to attach a picture. The image is displayed on the booking page and in the public listings list. Supported formats are JPEG, PNG, and WebP.
guide.q.add_file_attachment: How do I add a file attachment to a listing?
guide.a.add_file_attachment:
When creating or editing a listing, use the attachment upload field to attach a file. This can be any type of file — PDFs, Word documents, spreadsheets, images, audio, video, zip archives, you name it. The maximum file size is 25 MB.

Attendees see a download link on their ticket page. The link is time-limited and unique to each attendee, so it can't be shared or reused by others. Each time an attendee visits their ticket page, they get a fresh link that works for a short window.

To remove an attachment, open the listing and click Delete next to the current file name.
guide.q.listing_qr_code: Where can I find the listing QR code?
guide.a.listing_qr_code: On the admin listing page, click the QR code link next to the public URL. This opens an SVG image of the QR code that links to your listing's registration page. You can save or print it for posters, flyers, or other materials.
guide.q.duplicate_listing: How do I duplicate a listing?
guide.a.duplicate_listing: Open the listing and click Duplicate. This creates a new listing pre-filled with the same capacity, price, fields, group, and other settings so you can adjust what you need without starting from scratch. The name is left blank for you to fill in, and the image, attachment, and assigned questions are not copied.
guide.q.deactivate_listing: How do I deactivate a listing?
guide.a.deactivate_listing: Open the listing and click Deactivate. Deactivated listings no longer accept bookings and are hidden from the public listings list, but all existing attendee data is kept. Click Reactivate to make the listing bookable again.
guide.a.non_transferable_tickets: When you enable Non-Transferable on a listing, attendees see a notice on their ticket saying "Non-transferable — ID required at entry". At check-in, the QR scanner prompts door staff to verify the attendee's ID matches the name on the ticket before completing check-in. This helps prevent ticket touting.
guide.q.edit_attendee: How do I edit an attendee?
guide.a.edit_attendee:
Open the listing's attendee list, find the attendee, and click Edit. The edit page has three sections:

  • Contact Information — name, email, phone, address, special instructions, and custom question answers. These are shared across all the attendee's listing registrations.
  • Listing Registrations — a table showing each listing the attendee is registered for, with their quantity, check-in status, and refund status. You can update the quantity per listing or remove a registration.
  • Add to Listing — link the attendee to an additional listing. For daily listings, you also pick a date. Capacity is checked when adding.
guide.q.add_terms_and_conditions: How do I add terms and conditions?
guide.a.add_terms_and_conditions: In Settings, enter your terms in the "Terms and Conditions" box. When set, attendees must tick an agreement checkbox before they can reserve tickets. Clear the box to remove the requirement.
guide.a.what_are_custom_booking_question: Custom booking questions let you ask attendees a multiple-choice question during the booking process. Each question has a set of answers you define, and the attendee must select one before they can complete their booking.
guide.q.create_question: How do I create a question?
guide.a.create_question: Open any listing and click Questions in the listing menu, then follow the Manage Questions link. Type your question text and click Add Question. Then open the question and add your answer options. You can reorder answers using the move-up and move-down buttons.
guide.q.add_question_to_listing: How do I add a question to a listing?
guide.a.add_question_to_listing: Open the listing in the admin area and click Questions. Tick the questions you want to appear on that listing's booking form and save. The same question can be shared across multiple listings — create it once and assign it wherever you need it.
guide.q.share_questions_between_listings: Can I share questions between listings?
guide.a.share_questions_between_listings: Yes. Questions are created independently and then assigned to listings, so a single question can appear on as many listings as you like. Updating the question text or answers updates it everywhere it's used.
guide.q.where_to_see_answers: Where do I see the answers?
guide.a.where_to_see_answers: Answers appear in the attendee table on listing and group pages, so you can see at a glance what each attendee chose. They're also shown on the individual attendee detail page and included in the CSV export.
guide.q.facebook_403_error: Why do I get a 403 error when sharing my link on Facebook?
guide.a.facebook_403_error:
When you first share a link from a new domain on Facebook, Facebook may return a 403 error. This is because Facebook doesn't recognise the domain yet — the error comes from Facebook itself and doesn't even reach your site.

To fix this, paste your public link into the Facebook Sharing Debugger and click Scrape Again if the result looks wrong. Once Facebook has successfully scraped the URL, future shares should work normally.
guide.a.what_is_public_site: When enabled in Settings, your domain shows a public website with navigation for Home and Listings, plus T&Cs and Contact links if you've set those up. The Listings page lists all active listings with booking links. Visitors can browse listing details and book directly. If the public site is disabled, visitors can still book via direct ticket links.
guide.q.hide_listing_from_public_list: Can I hide a listing from the public list?
guide.a.hide_listing_from_public_list: Yes. When editing a listing, tick the Hidden Listing checkbox. Hidden listings won't appear on the public Listings page and their ticket pages will be marked as noindex, nofollow for search engines. The listing is still fully bookable via its direct link or when embedded in an iframe.
guide.q.edit_homepage_and_contact: How do I edit the homepage and contact page?
guide.a.edit_homepage_and_contact: Enable the public site in Settings, then open the Site section from the admin navigation. The homepage editor lets you set a website title (shown as the heading on all public pages) and homepage text. The contact page editor lets you set contact information. Both fields support Markdown formatting.
guide.a.what_is_purchase_only_mode:
When you enable No check-in on a listing, buyers can purchase the item without receiving an entry ticket — ideal for raffles, fundraisers, donations, merchandise, digital products, or anything else that does not need door scanning. The booking button changes from “Reserve” to “Buy now”, and after purchase buyers see “Your Purchase” instead of “Your Tickets”.

Because nobody needs to be checked in, QR codes, the check-in scanner, and wallet passes (Apple & Google) are all hidden. The listing is also excluded from the ICS and RSS feeds. Non-transferable ID notices are suppressed too, since there is no door to check at.
guide.q.how_do_i_merge_duplicate_attende: How do I merge duplicate attendees?
guide.a.how_do_i_merge_duplicate_attende:
If the same person booked separately and ended up with two attendee records, you can merge them. Open one attendee's edit page and find the Merge section. Enter the other attendee's ticket token to start the merge.

You'll see a comparison of their contact details, custom question answers, and listing registrations. For each conflict — where the two records differ — choose which value to keep. Non-conflicting data (e.g. an answer only one of them provided) is adopted automatically. Once confirmed, the source attendee is deleted and all chosen data is merged into the target.
guide.q.how_do_i_add_an_attendee_to: How do I add an attendee to another listing?
guide.a.how_do_i_add_an_attendee_to: Open the attendee's edit page and use the Add to Listing section at the bottom. Select the listing, choose a quantity, and for daily listings pick a date. If the listing has enough capacity the attendee is linked immediately.
guide.q.how_do_i_remove_an_attendee_from: How do I remove an attendee from a listing?
guide.a.how_do_i_remove_an_attendee_from: On the attendee's edit page, find the listing in the Listing Registrations table and click Remove. If the attendee is registered for other listings they stay in the system. If it was their only listing, the attendee is deleted entirely.
guide.q.how_do_i_delete_an_attendee: How do I delete an attendee?
guide.a.how_do_i_delete_an_attendee:
Open the listing's attendee list and click Delete next to the attendee. You'll see a confirmation page showing their name, email, quantity, and registration date. Type the attendee's exact name to confirm, then click Delete Attendee. This permanently removes the attendee and any associated payment records.

If the attendee has paid, refund them first before deleting — once deleted, there is no payment record to refund against. See the Refunds section below.
guide.q.how_do_i_resend_a_confirmation_e: How do I resend a confirmation email?
guide.a.how_do_i_resend_a_confirmation_e: In the listing's attendee list, click Re-send Notification next to the attendee. You'll be asked to type their name to confirm. This re-sends both the attendee confirmation email (with their ticket link) and the admin notification email. If email is not configured or the attendee has no email address, the action completes silently without sending.
guide.q.listing_in_multiple_groups: Can a listing be in more than one group?
guide.a.listing_in_multiple_groups: Yes. A listing's group membership is a set of checkboxes on its edit form, not a single choice — tick every group it should belong to. The same listing can appear on several group pages, and when a group is sold as a package it can carry a different package price in each one.
guide.a.what_are_listing_defaults:
Open Listing Defaults (owner only) to set values new listings inherit — bookable days, minimum notice, maximum days ahead, webhook and thank-you URLs, and whether new listings are hidden. Each listing has a single Use defaults switch; while it is on, those fields are hidden on that listing and follow the defaults.

Defaults apply live, not copied: change one here and every listing with Use defaults on updates automatically. Leave a field as No default to keep deciding it per listing.
guide.q.listing_page_tabs: Where do I find a listing's attendees, QR code and actions?
guide.a.listing_page_tabs: Each listing (and each attendee) opens as one page with a row of tabs across the top. A listing's tabs are Overview, Attendees, Edit, Questions, Booking QR, Activity and Actions (duplicate, export, scanner, refund all, deactivate, delete). You only see the tabs your role can open, so an editor lands straight on Edit.
guide.a.what_are_add_ons:
A listing can require the buyer to choose from a set of other listings when booking — one child for each unit they book. Set them on the listing's Edit tab under Advanced settings → Required child listings: tick the listings to offer, then Save required children. Children take the parent's date and duration, and a child can be offered under more than one parent.

Nesting is one level deep — a child can't itself have children, and a daily child needs a daily parent.
guide.q.bookable_alone: What does “Can Be Booked By Itself” mean?
guide.a.bookable_alone: By default, once a listing is used as another listing's child it loses its own booking page — buyers can only reach it inside the parent's flow. Tick Can Be Booked By Itself on the child's edit form to keep its own booking page, catalogue card and API eligibility as well as offering it as an add-on. Leave it off for an extra or upgrade that should only ever be sold alongside its parent.
guide.q.modifier_value_precision: What amounts can I enter for a modifier's value?
guide.a.modifier_value_precision: Enter a fixed Value and the optional Minimum order in your own currency (e.g. 10.00), to the number of decimal places that currency uses. An over-precise amount is now rejected with a validation error rather than silently rounded. Percentage and multiplier modifiers aren't currency amounts, so they keep their full precision.
guide.q.question_descriptions: Can a booking question have a longer description?
guide.a.question_descriptions: Yes. The Question Text field accepts markdown, so a question can include bold text, links, lists or several paragraphs. A short single line still renders inline as the field's label; a longer, formatted description renders as a prose block above the input, correctly labelled for screen readers.
guide.a.what_are_site_pages: Pages are your own content pages — a title, a markdown body and optional SEO title/description — that live at a public URL and can list chosen listings, groups and sub-pages. Manage them under Site → Pages.
guide.q.build_site_page: How do I build a Page and add it to the menu?
guide.a.build_site_page: Go to Site → Pages and choose Add Page. On the page's edit screen, use Add to this page to attach listings, groups or other pages, and reorder or remove them under Contents. Top-level pages appear in your site navigation (reorder them on the list); a page becomes a sub-page by being added to another page, and the public menu renders that hierarchy recursively. Deleting a page promotes its sub-pages to top level.
guide.q.news_posts: How do I post news on my public site?
guide.a.news_posts:
Open Site → News to write news posts. Each post has a name, an optional short snippet, optional SEO fields, and a Markdown body, and you can attach images from your image library — the first image becomes the post's picture, and extra images show as a small gallery under it.

Once at least one post exists, the public site shows a News link to /news, which lists every post with its name, snippet, and picture, newest first. A news RSS feed is available at /feeds/news.rss so readers can subscribe.
guide.q.group_vs_package: What's the difference between a group and a package?
guide.a.group_vs_package: A plain group simply shows several listings on one shared page. A package is a group with Sell this group as a package turned on: it is booked as a single bundle. Each member listing gets its own per-unit price and a fixed quantity included in one package, and the buyer chooses how many packages to book. Pay-what-you-want listings can't be packaged.
guide.q.sell_group_as_package: How do I sell a group as a package?
guide.a.sell_group_as_package: Create the group and add its listings, then open the group's Edit form and tick Sell this group as a package. A Package prices table appears with one row per member. Set each member's Per-unit price and Qty per package, then save. Customisable-days members also show a per-day price input for each booking length.
guide.q.package_member_pricing: How do per-member package prices and quantities work?
guide.a.package_member_pricing: For each member: leave Per-unit price blank to charge the listing's own price (shown as the placeholder), enter 0 to make it free inside this package, or enter an amount to override its price for this package only. Qty per package is how many of that listing one package includes (at least 1). Overrides are stored per group, so the same listing can be priced differently in different packages.
guide.q.hide_package_listings: How do I hide the listings inside a package?
guide.a.hide_package_listings:
Tick Hide the package's listings from buyers on the group's edit form. Buyers, tickets and confirmation emails then show only the package name — never the individual listings inside it — while admins still see the full breakdown. This is separate from Hide from public listings list, which only keeps the group off the public index but still reveals its members.

Once a hidden package has sold tickets you must un-hide it before un-grouping or deleting it, so existing tickets don't suddenly expose the concealed listings.
guide.q.package_capacity: How do I cap total bookings on a package?
guide.a.package_capacity: Set Max Attendees on the group. It limits the combined attendee count across every listing in the group, not each listing separately. The group's detail page shows a Group Attendees row with the current count, the cap, and how many remain.
